chapter: Trumpet players of the old days
title: Sugar Johnny, Roy Palmer, Harrison Ball and Sam Baldwin
summary: Gabriel describes trumpeters Sugar Johnny, Roy Palmer, Harrison Ball, and Sam Baldwin's band.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Yeah, I never got to knowing that.

He was a good trumpet player. Yeah, I've heard about him. I played in the band with him too, drummer. I don't play in the band with Sugar Johnny. Sugar Johnny was a nice trumpet player. He played with Roy Palmer.
I knew Roy Palmer. Roy Palmer, I played with him too.

Roy Palmer. He played trumpet and tramo. He learned Kedora Ney. People will know that, but he learned Kedora Ney a whole lot. Roy Palmer. He was right down there on the Georgia Martin corner. Roy would have him tall, skinny, dark man, Roy Palmer. He died about two years ago. He used to play in the band with my daddy, Roy Palmer. Look, it's alright if you want to stop. It's alright. Do you want to go and answer the phone? Who is it, boy, though? What were you talking about? Some trumpet players. Oh, Roy Palmer. Yeah, Roy Palmer.
Yeah, Roy Palmer. He was nice. How to build their leg.
You know Lego? No. Don't think so. Oh, yes.
He died. He was a trumpet player too. Play trombone and baritone. Oh, Roy Palmer. Roy Palmer, he was nice. You know Lego?
No, I don't think so. You know Harrison Ball?
Oh yes. He was a trumpet player too.
He played trombone in the baritone.

When I played with Sam Baldwin, all that music Sam couldn't play, then they hired him to play it. And some trombone player played in his place, and he'd pick up the trumpet and play all them numbers that Sam couldn't play. That trombone blues and all the music, he played all the music, that man, he was a good trumpet player.
